Δ={(u,v)\,:\,1\le u\le \sqrt{2},\,\,\frac{\pi }{6}\le v\le \frac{\pi }{3}},

and the transformation $T,$ given by

after.worked_solution:
To map the entire region $Δ$ onto the $xy$-plane, we consider the transformation of each side. However, in this case, we consider only the bottom side.

For the bottom side, we have $v=\frac{\pi }{6}$ and $1\le u\le \sqrt{2}.$ 

Substituting $v=\frac{\pi }{6}$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) \\  & =(u\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡v) \\  & =(u\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}),\,u\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})),\,\frac{\pi }{6}\le v\le \frac{\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

This is a parametric equation of the line segment shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14071828/assets/fcfc165548d8174ec0468dce53317fd0c8daa14565852c5e44d6764161723bed.png)

 

Note that the line that this segment lies on passes through the origin. 

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

- Statement I is true, while statement II is false. The slope of the line is

$$
k=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})}{\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})}=\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}).
$$

As a result, our line makes an angle of $\frac{\pi }{6}$ radians with the positive $x$-axis.

- Statement III is false.

- When $u=1,$ we obtain the point 
$(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})),$
whose distance to the origin is $1.$

- When $u=\sqrt{2},$ we obtain the point 
$(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}),\,\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})),$
whose distance to the origin is $\sqrt{2}.$

So, the endpoints of the line segment lie on the circles of radii $1$ and $\sqrt{2}.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."

This line segment makes an angle of $\frac{\pi }{6}$ with the positive $x$-axis in the $xy$-plane. Moreover, this segment lies on a line that passes through the origin, and its endpoints lie on the circles of radii $1$ and $3$ centered at $O.$
